## COMPLEMENT DEFICIENCY
Complement deficiency can be inherited or acquired. Acquired defects are
usually a consequence of other diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus.
Complement deficiency leads to increased rates of infections, usually of the
upper respiratory tract, but also occasionally with bacteremia or meningitis.
Pathogens are usually Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and
Neisseria gonorrhea.
Patients presenting with fever or other symptoms suggesting systemic bacterial
infection should be treated immediately with antimicrobials active against these
pathogens.
## Preferred empirical treatment
## Inpatient

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($5.71/day) [M]](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)
## Alternative for severe penicillin allergy
Chloramphenicol is not currently available. Contact Infectious Diseases for
advice.
## Outpatient

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.
